taxonomic_note: Accepted Tragia brevispica Engelm. & A.Gray under the current project treatment.
look_here_first: Look first at the short reproductive spike and then the leaves. Photograph or inspect the whole raceme with scale because this species can disappear among other stinging Tragia when only vegetative characters are used.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis is locked by University of Michigan specimen 1645723; Bexar by New York herbarium specimen evidence; Comal by 1846–47 Lindheimer material from New Braunfels after reconciling the historical locality to Comal County.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: The Comal assignment is tied to the dated New Braunfels locality after county-history reconciliation; do not generalize other undated historical localities.

best_field_traits: reproductive measurements and raceme architecture are more reliable than general habit
mature fruit is a small 3-lobed capsule typical of the genus
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use the short raceme together with bract, pedicel, leaf-proportion, and fruit characters; vegetative habit alone is not secure.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use the short raceme together with bract, pedicel, leaf-proportion, and fruit characters; vegetative habit alone is not secure.

photo_note: Photo-first curation underway. Candidate set now covers leaf+fruit, stinging hairs, raceme/flower arrangement, mature fruit, whole specimen, and a Central Texas live observation. learner_visual_status.note: Temporary one-photo learner coverage. Keep until stronger diagnostic gallery coverage replaces or supplements it.

visual_learning.learner_goal: Recognize this as a stinging Tragia first, then prove brevispica from the reproductive axis rather than from general habit.

look_sequence.question: Does the plant fit the stinging-hair Tragia door?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Use a macro view. Do not handle bare-handed just to test the character.

look_sequence.look_at: leaf base, margin and overall blade proportions
look_sequence.question: What is the leaf architecture?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Frame one mature leaf flat enough to compare its base, margin and length:width relationship with other Tragia.

look_sequence.question: Is the reproductive axis genuinely short, and how are the flowers distributed along it?
look_sequence.teaching_note: This is the primary species-level visual lock currently supported by the project. Include a ruler or other scale reference when possible.

look_sequence.look_at: bracts, pedicels and staminate versus pistillate flowers
look_sequence.question: Where are the male and female flowers, and what are their attachment details?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Use a side-on macro that keeps bract and pedicel visible instead of a flower-only beauty shot.

look_sequence.question: Does the plant show the expected small 3-lobed Tragia capsule, and what fruit characters can be compared?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Photograph a mature capsule in side view with scale; fruit is more useful than overall scrambling habit.

comparison_board.warning: Do not separate these from habit alone.
A wide habit shot is supporting context; reproductive structure should carry the comparison.
Habitat can support an identification but should not replace reproductive characters.

photo_diagram_needs.annotation: bracket the reproductive axis; mark basal and terminal ends
label male vs female flowers plus bract and pedicel
arrow to individual stinging hairs; add handling caution
mark leaf base, margin and length:width axis
use arrows to show where leaf, raceme and fruit details occur on the specimen

avoid_overtrusting: a single leaf shape without reproductive material
the presence of stinging hairs as a species-level character
habitat as a substitute for reproductive structure

verified_diagnostic_anchors.raceme_architecture: racemelike; one (occasionally two) pistillate flower low on the axis with several staminate flowers above
verified_diagnostic_anchors.mature_fruit: capsule about 6.5–7 mm wide; often only one carpel matures
verified_diagnostic_anchors.leaf: triangular to cordate with serrate to crenate margin; stinging hairs can be conspicuous, including near margins/basal lobes
source_basis: UT Austin PRC Williamson County treatment
